decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_ratios`, first half.** `λ_{2j} ≥ λ_j ε(j)`: the doubling edge out of `j` deposits at least its own share at `2j`, whatever else arrives there.

decls.name: Stat.lam_le_prev
decls.statement: theorem Stat.lam_le_prev (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : L.lam (.lad m) * (1 - S.eps m) ≤ L.lam (.lad (m - 1))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_ratios`, second half.** `λ_m (1 − ε(m)) ≤ λ_{m−1}`.

files.title: From the `L²(λ)` Rayleigh inequality to the mass layer
variables: variable {S : Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : Stat S cap)

decls.name: memLp_two_of_bounded
decls.statement: theorem memLp_two_of_bounded {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : MemLp f 2 L.mu
decls.doc: A bounded function is in `L²(λ)`: `λ` is a probability.

decls.name: norm_sq_eq_mass_of_ae
decls.statement: theorem norm_sq_eq_mass_of_ae {F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} {g : St → ℝ} (h : ⇑F =ᵐ[L.mu] g) (hg : MemLp g 2 L.mu) : ‖F‖ ^ 2 = L.mass 2 g
decls.doc: The `L²` norm squared of a class is the `mass` of any of its representatives, at every `cap`.

decls.name: tsum_lam_mul_congr_ae
decls.statement: theorem tsum_lam_mul_congr_ae {F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} {g : St → ℝ} (h : ⇑F =ᵐ[L.mu] g) : ∑' x, L.lam x * (F : St → ℝ) x = ∑' x, L.lam x * g x
decls.doc: The `λ`-mean of a class is the `λ`-mean of any of its representatives, at every `cap`.

decls.name: coeFn_sub_pstarL2_toLp
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_sub_pstarL2_toLp (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : MemLp f 2 L.mu) : ⇑(hf.toLp f - L.pstarL2 hrow (hf.toLp f)) =ᵐ[L.mu] fun x => f x - pstar S cap f x
decls.doc: The defect class of the class of `f` is the class of the pointwise defect.

decls.name: rayleigh_of_leftInverse
decls.statement: theorem rayleigh_of_leftInverse (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {Sop : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} (hS : Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ‖F - L.piL2 F‖ ≤ ‖Sop‖ * ‖F - L.pstarL2 hrow F‖
decls.doc: A bounded left inverse `S` of `Id − P⋆` on `L²(λ)`, `S(Id − P⋆) = Id − Π`, bounds the mean-zero part of every class by `‖S‖` times its defect.

decls.name: mass_le_of_rayleighL2
decls.statement: theorem mass_le_of_rayleighL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {B : ℝ} (hB : ∀ F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu, ‖F - L.piL2 F‖ ≤ B * ‖F - L.pstarL2 hrow F‖) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) (hmean : ∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) : L.mass 2 f ≤ B ^ 2 * L.mass 2 (fun x => f x - pstar S cap f x)
decls.doc: **The bridge.** If `‖F − ΠF‖ ≤ B‖F − P⋆F‖` on `L²(λ)`, then every bounded mean-zero `f` has `mass 2 f ≤ B² · mass 2 ((Id − P⋆)f)`.

decls.name: mass_le_of_leftInverse
decls.statement: theorem mass_le_of_leftInverse (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {Sop : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} (hS : Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 hrow) = 1 - L.piL2) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) (hmean : ∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) : L.mass 2 f ≤ ‖Sop‖ ^ 2 * L.mass 2 (fun x => f x - pstar S cap f x)
decls.doc: The bridge, fed by a left inverse: `mass 2 f ≤ ‖S‖² · mass 2 ((Id − P⋆)f)`.

files.title: The renewal form of the cut balance, and the two constants written `B̂`
variables: variable {k V : ℝ → ℝ} {K0 K1 M : ℝ}
variable {c p : ℝ} {V : ℝ → ℝ} {M : ℝ}
variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam : V → ℝ}
variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {Q : E →L[ℝ] E}

decls.name: kern
decls.statement: noncomputable def kern (c p v : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The kernel `k(v) = c ln 2 · 2^{p v}` of `lem:doubling_cramer_root`(2).

decls.name: continuous_kern
decls.statement: theorem continuous_kern (c p : ℝ) : Continuous (kern c p)

decls.name: hasDerivAt_kern
decls.statement: theorem hasDerivAt_kern (c p v : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (kern c p) (c * log 2 * ((2 : ℝ) ^ (p * v) * log 2 * p)) v

decls.name: kern_pos
decls.statement: theorem kern_pos {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (p v : ℝ) : 0 < kern c p v

decls.name: two_rpow_mul_le
decls.statement: theorem two_rpow_mul_le {p v : ℝ} (hv : v ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : (2 : ℝ) ^ (p * v) ≤ 1 + (2 : ℝ) ^ p

decls.name: kernSup
decls.statement: noncomputable def kernSup (c p : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The explicit sup bound of the kernel on `[0,1]`: `K₀ := c ln 2 (1 + τ)`.

decls.name: kernLip
decls.statement: noncomputable def kernLip (c p : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The explicit Lipschitz constant of the kernel on `[0,1]`: `K₁ := c (ln 2)² |p| (1 + τ)`.

decls.name: abs_kern_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_kern_le {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (p : ℝ) {v : ℝ} (hv : v ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : |kern c p v| ≤ kernSup c p
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, "`k` being bounded … on `[0,1]`"**: `|k(v)| ≤ c ln 2 (1 + τ)`.

decls.name: kernLip_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem kernLip_nonneg {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (p : ℝ) : 0 ≤ kernLip c p

decls.name: abs_kern_sub_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_kern_sub_le {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (p : ℝ) {u v : ℝ} (hu : u ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) (hv : v ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : |kern c p u - kern c p v| ≤ kernLip c p * |u - v|
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, the kernel is Lipschitz on `[0,1]`**, with constant `c (ln 2)² |p| (1 + τ)` — the form in which its regularity enters `conv_lipschitz`.

decls.name: kern_boundedVariationOn
decls.statement: theorem kern_boundedVariationOn {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (p : ℝ) : BoundedVariationOn (kern c p) (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, "`k` being … of bounded variation on `[0,1]`"** — it is Lipschitz there.

decls.name: intervalIntegrable_of_abs_le
decls.statement: theorem intervalIntegrable_of_abs_le {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Measurable f) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ M) (a b : ℝ) : IntervalIntegrable f volume a b
decls.doc: A bounded measurable function is interval integrable on every interval.

decls.name: intervalIntegrable_mul_shift
decls.statement: theorem intervalIntegrable_mul_shift (hk : Continuous k) (hV : Measurable V) (hM : ∀ x, |V x| ≤ M) (x a b : ℝ) : IntervalIntegrable (fun u => k u * V (x - u)) volume a b

decls.name: intervalIntegrable_mul_shift'
decls.statement: theorem intervalIntegrable_mul_shift' (hk : Continuous k) (hV : Measurable V) (hM : ∀ x, |V x| ≤ M) (x h a b : ℝ) : IntervalIntegrable (fun u => k (u + h) * V (x - u)) volume a b

decls.name: conv_sub_le
decls.statement: theorem conv_sub_le (hk : Continuous k) (hK0 : ∀ v ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, |k v| ≤ K0) (hK1 : 0 ≤ K1) (hK1' : ∀ u ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ v ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, |k u - k v| ≤ K1 * |u - v|) (hV : Measurable V) (hM : ∀ x, |V x| ≤ M) (x : ℝ) {h : ℝ} (hh : 0 ≤ h) : |(∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, k v * V (x + h - v)) - ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, k v * V (x - v)| ≤ M * (2 * K0 + K1) * h
decls.doc: The one-sided estimate behind the Lipschitz bound: for `0 ≤ h`, `|F(x+h) − F(x)| ≤ M(2K₀ + K₁)h` with `F(x) = ∫₀¹ k(v)V(x−v)dv`.

decls.name: conv_lipschitz
decls.statement: theorem conv_lipschitz (hk : Continuous k) (hK0 : ∀ v ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, |k v| ≤ K0) (hK1 : 0 ≤ K1) (hK1' : ∀ u ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ v ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, |k u - k v| ≤ K1 * |u - v|) (hV : Measurable V) (hM : ∀ x, |V x| ≤ M) : LipschitzWith (Real.toNNReal (M * (2 * K0 + K1))) (fun x => ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, k v * V (x - v))
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, "the right side is Lipschitz in `x`, `k` being bounded and of bounded variation on `[0,1]` and `V` bounded"**, for a kernel bounded by `K₀` and `K₁`-Lipschitz on `[0,1]`: `x ↦ ∫₀¹ k(v)V(x−v)dv` is `M(2K₀ + K₁)`-Lipschitz.

decls.name: integral_kern
decls.statement: theorem integral_kern (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kern c p v = 1
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, "whose normalization `∫₀¹ k = 1` is the Cramér relation"**: the kernel of `lem:doubling_cramer_root`(2) integrates to `1` at a root of `ψ` (`cramer_kernel_integral`).

decls.name: kbar
decls.statement: noncomputable def kbar (c p v : ℝ) : ℝ

decls.name: kbar_zero
decls.statement: theorem kbar_zero (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : kbar c p 0 = 1
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, `k̄(0) = 1`** — the Cramér relation again.

decls.name: kbar_one
decls.statement: theorem kbar_one : kbar c p 1 = 0
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, `k̄(1) = 0`**.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_kbar
decls.statement: theorem hasDerivAt_kbar (v : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (kbar c p) (-kern c p v) v
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, `k̄' = −k`**, at every `v`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_two_rpow_mul
decls.statement: theorem hasDerivAt_two_rpow_mul (p w : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (fun v : ℝ => (2 : ℝ) ^ (p * v)) ((2 : ℝ) ^ (p * w) * log 2 * p) w
decls.doc: `2^{p·w}` has derivative `2^{p·w} ln 2 · p`.

decls.name: kbar_eq
decls.statement: theorem kbar_eq (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (v : ℝ) : kbar c p v = c / p * ((2 : ℝ) ^ p - (2 : ℝ) ^ (p * v))
decls.doc: The closed form `k̄(v) = (c/p)(τ − 2^{p v})`.

decls.name: continuous_kbar
decls.statement: theorem continuous_kbar (c p : ℝ) : Continuous (kbar c p)

decls.name: Gfun
decls.statement: noncomputable def Gfun (c p : ℝ) (V : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `G(x) := ∫₀¹ k̄(v) V(x − v) dv`, the leftmost expression of the remark's display.

decls.name: Gfun_eq_shift
decls.statement: theorem Gfun_eq_shift (V : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : Gfun c p V x = ∫ y in (x - 1)..x, kbar c p (x - y) * V y
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, the two expressions of `G` agree**: `∫₀¹ k̄(v)V(x−v)dv = ∫_{x−1}^x k̄(x−y)V(y)dy`.

decls.name: rhs_eq_shift
decls.statement: theorem rhs_eq_shift (V : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : (∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kern c p v * V (x - v)) = ∫ y in (x - 1)..x, kern c p (x - y) * V y
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, the right side of the limit equation, in both forms**: `∫₀¹ k(v)V(x−v)dv = ∫_{x−1}^x k(x−y)V(y)dy`.

decls.name: renewal_rhs_lipschitz
decls.statement: theorem renewal_rhs_lipschitz (hc : 0 < c) (hVm : Measurable V) (hM : ∀ x, |V x| ≤ M) : LipschitzWith (Real.toNNReal (M * (2 * kernSup c p + kernLip c p))) (fun x => ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kern c p v * V (x - v))
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, the Lipschitz sentence, first half**: for bounded measurable `V`, the right side `x ↦ ∫₀¹ k(v)V(x−v)dv` of the limit equation is Lipschitz, with the explicit constant `M(2K₀ + K₁)`, `K₀ = c ln 2 (1+τ)` and `K₁ = c (ln 2)² |p| (1+τ)`.

decls.name: renewal_lipschitz
decls.statement: theorem renewal_lipschitz (hc : 0 < c) (hVm : Measurable V) (hM : ∀ x, |V x| ≤ M) (heq : ∀ x, V x = ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kern c p v * V (x - v)) : LipschitzWith (Real.toNNReal (M * (2 * kernSup c p + kernLip c p))) V
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, the Lipschitz sentence, second half**: a bounded measurable solution `V` of the limit equation `V(x) = ∫₀¹ k(v)V(x−v)dv` is Lipschitz, with the same constant.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_Gfun
decls.statement: theorem hasDerivAt_Gfun (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hVc : Continuous V) (x : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (Gfun c p V) (kbar c p 0 * V x - kbar c p 1 * V (x - 1) - ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kern c p v * V (x - v)) x
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, the Leibniz computation of the display**, for continuous `V`: `G'(x) = k̄(0)V(x) − k̄(1)V(x−1) − ∫₀¹ k(v)V(x−v)dv`, at every `x`.

decls.name: renewal_hasDerivAt_G
decls.statement: theorem renewal_hasDerivAt_G (hc : 0 < c) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) (hVm : Measurable V) (hM : ∀ x, |V x| ≤ M) (heq : ∀ x, V x = ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kern c p v * V (x - v)) (x : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (Gfun c p V) (kbar c p 0 * V x - kbar c p 1 * V (x - 1) - ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kern c p v * V (x - v)) x ∧ kbar c p 0 * V x - kbar c p 1 * V (x - 1) - ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kern c p v * V (x - v) = 0
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, `G' = 0`**: for a bounded measurable solution `V` of the limit equation, `G'(x) = k̄(0)V(x) − k̄(1)V(x−1) − ∫₀¹ k(v)V(x−v)dv = 0` at every `x`.

decls.name: renewal_G_const
decls.statement: theorem renewal_G_const (hc : 0 < c) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) (hVm : Measurable V) (hM : ∀ x, |V x| ≤ M) (heq : ∀ x, V x = ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kern c p v * V (x - v)) (x y : ℝ) : Gfun c p V x = Gfun c p V y
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, "so `G` is constant"**.

decls.name: kernMean
decls.statement: noncomputable def kernMean (c p : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The mean of the kernel, `∫₀¹ v k(v) dv`.

decls.name: integral_kbar_eq_kernMean
decls.statement: theorem integral_kbar_eq_kernMean (hp0 : p ≠ 0) : (∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kbar c p v) = kernMean c p ∧ kernMean c p = c / p * ((2 : ℝ) ^ p - ((2 : ℝ) ^ p - 1) / (p * log 2))
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, `∫₀¹ k̄ = ∫₀¹ v k(v) dv`**, both in closed form: `(c/p)(τ − (τ−1)/(p ln 2))`.

decls.name: kernMean_eq
decls.statement: theorem kernMean_eq (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : kernMean c p = deriv (psi c) p / (p * log 2) ∧ kernMean c p = (2 : ℝ) ^ p / ((2 : ℝ) ^ p - 1) - 1 / (p * log 2)
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, the mean of the kernel is `ψ'(p_*)/(p_* ln 2) = τ/(τ−1) − 1/(p_* ln 2)`**, by the Cramér relation `eq:doubling_cramer_form`.

decls.name: kernMean_pos
decls.statement: theorem kernMean_pos (hc : 0 < c) : 0 < kernMean c p
decls.doc: The mean of the kernel is positive, for `c > 0`.

decls.name: renewal_limit
decls.statement: theorem renewal_limit (hc : 0 < c) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) (hVm : Measurable V) (hM : ∀ x, |V x| ≤ M) (heq : ∀ x, V x = ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kern c p v * V (x - v)) {ℓ : ℝ} (hlim : Tendsto V atTop (𝓝 ℓ)) (x₀ : ℝ) : ℓ = Gfun c p V x₀ / ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kbar c p v
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, the limit**: if a bounded measurable solution `V` of the limit equation has a limit `ℓ` at `+∞`, then, dominated convergence in the leftmost expression of `G`, `ℓ = G / ∫₀¹ k̄` — with `∫₀¹ k̄ = ∫₀¹ v k(v) dv = ψ'(p_*)/(p_* ln 2) = τ/(τ−1) − 1/(p_* ln 2)` (`integral_kbar_eq_kernMean`, `kernMean_eq`).

decls.name: kernMeasure
decls.statement: noncomputable def kernMeasure (c p : ℝ) : Measure ℝ
decls.doc: The law with density `k` on `[0,1]`.

decls.name: kernMeasure_univ
decls.statement: theorem kernMeasure_univ (hc : 0 < c) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : kernMeasure c p univ = 1
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, `∫₀¹ k = 1` as a probability law**: the kernel is a probability density.

decls.name: kernMeasure_absolutelyContinuous
decls.statement: theorem kernMeasure_absolutelyContinuous (c p : ℝ) : kernMeasure c p ≪ volume
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, "that kernel has a density"**: its law is absolutely continuous.

decls.name: kernMeasure_nonlattice
decls.statement: theorem kernMeasure_nonlattice (hc : 0 < c) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) (a h : ℝ) : ¬ ∀ᵐ x ∂kernMeasure c p, ∃ n : ℤ, x = a + n * h
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_renewal`, "hence is non-lattice"**: no lattice `a + hℤ` carries the law, since it charges no countable set.

decls.name: const_isRenewalSolution
decls.statement: theorem const_isRenewalSolution (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) (ℓ x : ℝ) : (fun _ : ℝ => ℓ) x = ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kern c p v * (fun _ : ℝ => ℓ) (x - v)
decls.doc: **The limit equation is inhabited**: every constant is a bounded measurable solution.

decls.name: renewal_limit_check
decls.statement: theorem renewal_limit_check (ℓ : ℝ) : ∃ p : ℝ, p ≠ 0 ∧ psi (1 / 2) p = 0 ∧ ℓ = Gfun (1 / 2) p (fun _ => ℓ) 0 / ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, kbar (1 / 2) p v
decls.doc: **Non-vacuity check of `renewal_limit`**: at `c = 1/2` the Cramér root exists, and on the constant solution `V ≡ ℓ` the limit formula returns `ℓ`, `G ≡ ℓ ∫₀¹ k̄`.

decls.name: funAct_add'
decls.statement: theorem funAct_add' (K : V → V → ℝ) (a b : V → ℝ) : Core.funAct K (fun y => a y + b y) = fun x => Core.funAct K a x + Core.funAct K b x

decls.name: funAct_smul'
decls.statement: theorem funAct_smul' (K : V → V → ℝ) (c : ℝ) (a : V → ℝ) : Core.funAct K (fun y => c * a y) = fun x => c * Core.funAct K a x

decls.name: funLin
decls.statement: noncomputable def funLin (lam : V → ℝ) (K : V → V → ℝ) : EuclideanSpace ℝ V →ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ V
decls.doc: The function action `(P⋆f)(x) = ∑_y T(x→y)f(y)`, conjugated by the weighting, as a linear map on `L²(λ) ≅ EuclideanSpace ℝ V`.

decls.name: funOp
decls.statement: noncomputable def funOp (lam : V → ℝ) (K : V → V → ℝ) : EuclideanSpace ℝ V →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ V
decls.doc: `P⋆`, the function action, bundled on `L²(λ)`.

decls.name: funOp_wtL2
decls.statement: theorem funOp_wtL2 {lam : V → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) (K : V → V → ℝ) (a : V → ℝ) : funOp lam K (wtL2 lam a) = wtL2 lam (Core.funAct K a)

decls.name: funOp_pow_wtL2
decls.statement: theorem funOp_pow_wtL2 {lam : V → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) (K : V → V → ℝ) (a : V → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : (funOp lam K ^ n) (wtL2 lam a) = wtL2 lam ((Core.funAct K)^[n] a)

decls.name: inner_funOp
decls.statement: theorem inner_funOp {lam : V → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) (K : V → V → ℝ) (u v : EuclideanSpace ℝ V) : ⟪funOp lam K u, v⟫ = ⟪u, densOp lam K v⟫
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_two_constants`, the adjoint behind the ordering**: on a finite chain `P⋆` is the `L²(λ)`-adjoint of the density action `P`, `⟪P⋆u, v⟫ = ⟪u, Pv⟫` — the finite face of `lem:doubling_operator`(1).

decls.name: funOp_eq_star
decls.statement: theorem funOp_eq_star {lam : V → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) (K : V → V → ℝ) : funOp lam K = star (densOp lam K)

decls.name: meanOp_eq_star
decls.statement: theorem meanOp_eq_star {lam : V → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) : meanOp lam = star (meanOp lam)

decls.name: norm_funOp_pow_sub
decls.statement: theorem norm_funOp_pow_sub {lam : V → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) (K : V → V → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ‖funOp lam K ^ n - meanOp lam‖ = Core.Mixing.beta (densOp lam K) (meanOp lam) n
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_two_constants`, `‖P⋆ⁿ − Π‖ = β̂ₙ`** on a finite chain — the finite face of `lem:doubling_operator`(1).

decls.name: meanOp_mul_funOp
decls.statement: theorem meanOp_mul_funOp {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam : V → ℝ} (hinv : Core.IsInvariant lam K) (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) : meanOp lam * funOp lam K = meanOp lam
decls.doc: `Π P⋆ = Π`, the adjoint of `P Π = Π` (invariance of `λ`).

decls.name: funOp_mul_meanOp
decls.statement: theorem funOp_mul_meanOp {K : V → V → ℝ} {lam : V → ℝ} (hK : Core.IsMarkov K) (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) : funOp lam K * meanOp lam = meanOp lam
decls.doc: `P⋆ Π = Π`, the adjoint of `Π P = Π` (`T` is Markov).

decls.name: meanOp_mul_self
decls.statement: theorem meanOp_mul_self {lam : V → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) (htot : ∑ x, lam x = 1) : meanOp lam * meanOp lam = meanOp lam

decls.name: inverse_sub_eq_of_tendsto
decls.statement: theorem inverse_sub_eq_of_tendsto (hK : Core.IsMarkov K) (hinv : Core.IsInvariant lam K) (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) (htot : ∑ x, lam x = 1) {U : EuclideanSpace ℝ V →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ V} (hconv : Tendsto (partialSum (funOp lam K) (meanOp lam)) atTop (𝓝 U)) : IsUnit (1 - funOp lam K + meanOp lam) ∧ Ring.inverse (1 - funOp lam K + meanOp lam) - meanOp lam = U
decls.doc: When the partial sums of `Σ(P⋆ⁿ − Π)` converge in operator norm to `U`, `Id − P⋆ + Π` is a unit and the paper's `S = (Id − P⋆ + Π)^{-1} − Π` is `U`.

decls.name: bhat_le_mixing_sum
decls.statement: theorem bhat_le_mixing_sum (hK : Core.IsMarkov K) (hinv : Core.IsInvariant lam K) (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) (htot : ∑ x, lam x = 1) {B : ℝ} (hB : ∀ N : ℕ, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, Core.Mixing.beta (densOp lam K) (meanOp lam) n ≤ B) : ‖Ring.inverse (1 - funOp lam K + meanOp lam) - meanOp lam‖ ≤ B
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_two_constants`, "item (3) of `lem:doubling_operator` orders the two on any finite irreducible chain"**, on every finite chain with `λ > 0` its invariant probability: the norm `B̂ = ‖(Id − P⋆ + Π)^{-1} − Π‖` of the diffusion operator is at most every real `B` bounding the partial sums of the mixing sum `Σ β̂ₙ`, `β̂ₙ = ‖Pⁿ − Π‖` on the density action.

decls.name: diffusion_apply_eq_series
decls.statement: theorem diffusion_apply_eq_series (hK : Core.IsMarkov K) (hinv : Core.IsInvariant lam K) (hlam : ∀ x, 0 < lam x) (htot : ∑ x, lam x = 1) {U : EuclideanSpace ℝ V →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ V} (hconv : Tendsto (partialSum (funOp lam K) (meanOp lam)) atTop (𝓝 U)) (θ : V → ℝ) (x : V) : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, ((Core.funAct K)^[n] θ x - Graph.meanL2 lam θ)) atTop (𝓝 (unwtL2 lam ((Ring.inverse (1 - funOp lam K + meanOp lam) - meanOp lam) (wtL2 lam θ)) x))
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_two_constants`, the trajectory reading, as a pointwise series**: on a finite chain, wherever `Σ(P⋆ⁿ − Π)` converges in operator norm, `(Sθ)(x) = Σ_{n≥0}((P⋆ⁿθ)(x) − λ(θ))`, with `(P⋆ⁿθ)(x) = ∑_y Tⁿ(x→y)θ(y)` the `n`-fold function action, which the paper reads as `E(θ(Xₙ) | X₀ = x)` (not identified here).

decls.name: flipK
decls.statement: noncomputable def flipK (q : ℝ) : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → ℝ
decls.doc: The two-state chain that flips with probability `q`.

decls.name: flipK_isMarkov
decls.statement: theorem flipK_isMarkov (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1) : Core.IsMarkov (flipK q)

decls.name: flipK_isInvariant
decls.statement: theorem flipK_isInvariant (q : ℝ) : Core.IsInvariant twoStateLam (flipK q)

decls.name: flipK_invariant_unique
decls.statement: theorem flipK_invariant_unique (hq : q ≠ 0) {mu : Fin 2 → ℝ} (hinv : ∀ y, ∑ x, mu x * flipK q x y = mu y) (htot : ∑ x, mu x = 1) : mu = twoStateLam
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_two_constants`, "whose invariant probability is uniform"**: for `q ≠ 0` the uniform law is the only invariant probability of the flip chain.

decls.name: densOp_flipK
decls.statement: theorem densOp_flipK (q : ℝ) : densOp twoStateLam (flipK q) = meanOp twoStateLam + (1 - 2 * q) • (1 - meanOp twoStateLam)
decls.doc: The flip chain's operators, in terms of `Π`: `P = P⋆ = Π + (1 − 2q)(Id − Π)`.

decls.name: funOp_flipK
decls.statement: theorem funOp_flipK (q : ℝ) : funOp twoStateLam (flipK q) = meanOp twoStateLam + (1 - 2 * q) • (1 - meanOp twoStateLam)

decls.name: flipK_funAct_centred
decls.statement: theorem flipK_funAct_centred (q : ℝ) {f : Fin 2 → ℝ} (hf : Graph.meanL2 twoStateLam f = 0) : Core.funAct (flipK q) f = fun x => (1 - 2 * q) * f x
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_two_constants`, "centred functions are eigenfunctions of its transition operator"**, at the eigenvalue `1 − 2q` (`−1/2` at `q = 3/4`).

decls.name: mul_proj_add_smul
decls.statement: theorem mul_proj_add_smul (hQ : Q * Q = Q) (a b : ℝ) : (Q + a • (1 - Q)) * (Q + b • (1 - Q)) = Q + (a * b) • (1 - Q)
decls.doc: Operators of the form `Q + a(Id − Q)`, `Q` idempotent, multiply by multiplying `a`.

decls.name: pow_proj_add_smul
decls.statement: theorem pow_proj_add_smul (hQ : Q * Q = Q) (r : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : (Q + r • (1 - Q)) ^ n = Q + r ^ n • (1 - Q)

decls.name: beta_flipK
decls.statement: theorem beta_flipK (q : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Core.Mixing.beta (densOp twoStateLam (flipK q)) (meanOp twoStateLam) n = |1 - 2 * q| ^ n
decls.doc: `β̂ₙ = |1 − 2q|ⁿ` on the flip chain, with `β̂ₙ = ‖Pⁿ − Π‖` on the density action.

decls.name: mixing_flipK
decls.statement: theorem mixing_flipK (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) : Core.Mixing (densOp twoStateLam (flipK q)) (meanOp twoStateLam)
decls.doc: **Summable mixing exhibited** on the flip chain, `0 < q < 1`.

decls.name: B_flipK
decls.statement: theorem B_flipK (hq0 : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) : Core.Mixing.B (densOp twoStateLam (flipK q)) (meanOp twoStateLam) = (1 - |1 - 2 * q|)⁻¹
decls.doc: The mixing sum `Σ β̂ₙ = (1 − |1 − 2q|)⁻¹` on the flip chain, `0 < q < 1`.

decls.name: diffusion_flipK
decls.statement: theorem diffusion_flipK (hq : q ≠ 0) : Ring.inverse (1 - funOp twoStateLam (flipK q) + meanOp twoStateLam) - meanOp twoStateLam = (2 * q)⁻¹ • (1 - meanOp twoStateLam)
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_two_constants`, the diffusion operator of the flip chain**: `S = (Id − P⋆ + Π)^{-1} − Π = (2q)^{-1}(Id − Π)`, for `q ≠ 0`.

decls.name: norm_diffusion_flipK
decls.statement: theorem norm_diffusion_flipK {q : ℝ} (hq : 0 < q) : ‖Ring.inverse (1 - funOp twoStateLam (flipK q) + meanOp twoStateLam) - meanOp twoStateLam‖ = (2 * q)⁻¹
decls.doc: `‖S‖ = (2q)^{-1}` on the flip chain, `q > 0`.

decls.name: two_constants_flip_three_quarters
decls.statement: theorem two_constants_flip_three_quarters : (∀ mu : Fin 2 → ℝ, (∀ y, ∑ x, mu x * flipK (3 / 4) x y = mu y) → ∑ x, mu x = 1 → mu = twoStateLam) ∧ Core.IsInvariant twoStateLam (flipK (3 / 4)) ∧ (∀ f : Fin 2 → ℝ, Graph.meanL2 twoStateLam f = 0 → Core.funAct (flipK (3 / 4)) f = fun x => -(1 / 2) * f x) ∧ ‖Ring.inverse (1 - funOp twoStateLam (flipK (3 / 4)) + meanOp twoStateLam) - meanOp twoStateLam‖ = 2 / 3 ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, Core.Mixing.beta (densOp twoStateLam (flipK (3 / 4))) (meanOp twoStateLam) n = ((2 : ℝ) ^ n)⁻¹) ∧ Core.Mixing (densOp twoStateLam (flipK (3 / 4))) (meanOp twoStateLam) ∧ Core.Mixing.B (densOp twoStateLam (flipK (3 / 4))) (meanOp twoStateLam) = 2 ∧ ‖Ring.inverse (1 - funOp twoStateLam (flipK (3 / 4)) + meanOp twoStateLam) - meanOp twoStateLam‖ ≠ Core.Mixing.B (densOp twoStateLam (flipK (3 / 4))) (meanOp twoStateLam)
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_two_constants`, the witness**: on the two-state chain that flips with probability `3/4`, whose invariant probability is uniform and whose centred functions are eigenfunctions of its transition operator at `−1/2`, the diffusion constant is `B̂ = 2/3` while `β̂ₙ = 2^{-n}` for every `n ≥ 0` and `Σₙ β̂ₙ = 2`: the two constants written `B̂` do not coincide.

decls.name: two_constants_flip_half
decls.statement: theorem two_constants_flip_half : ‖Ring.inverse (1 - funOp twoStateLam (flipK (1 / 2)) + meanOp twoStateLam) - meanOp twoStateLam‖ = 1 ∧ Core.Mixing.B (densOp twoStateLam (flipK (1 / 2))) (meanOp twoStateLam) = 1
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_two_constants`, "at the flip probability `1/2` both equal `1`"**.

decls.name: flipK_half_eq_twoStateK
decls.statement: theorem flipK_half_eq_twoStateK : flipK (1 / 2) = twoStateK
decls.doc: The flip chain at `q = 1/2` is `Freezing.lean`'s `twoStateK`, the chain of `prop:nonlinear_freezing`(2), whose `B̂ = 1` is `twoState_B_densOp`.

decls.name: bhat_le_mixing_sum_check
decls.statement: theorem bhat_le_mixing_sum_check : ‖Ring.inverse (1 - funOp twoStateLam (flipK (3 / 4)) + meanOp twoStateLam) - meanOp twoStateLam‖ ≤ 2
decls.doc: **The ordering, checked on the witness**: `bhat_le_mixing_sum` applies to the flip chain at `3/4` (its hypotheses are met), and returns `2/3 ≤ 2`.

decls.name: diffusion_series_converges_check
decls.statement: theorem diffusion_series_converges_check : ∃ U : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), Tendsto (partialSum (funOp twoStateLam (flipK (3 / 4))) (meanOp twoStateLam)) atTop (𝓝 U)
decls.doc: **Non-vacuity of `diffusion_apply_eq_series`**: on the flip chain at `3/4` the series `Σ(P⋆ⁿ − Π)` converges in operator norm, so the trajectory reading applies there.

files.title: The doubling graph: state space, backward policy, and invariant sequences
variables: variable {S : Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} {f g : St → ℝ}
variable {S : Setting} {cap : Option ℕ} (L : Stat S cap)

decls.name: St
decls.statement: inductive St
decls.doc: The states of the doubling graph `eq:counterexample_graph`.

decls.name: src
decls.statement: @[match_pattern] abbrev src : St
decls.doc: The source `s₀`, which is the ladder index `0`.

decls.statement: instance : Countable St
decls.doc: `St` is countable: `lad j ↦ j + 1` and `sink ↦ 0` is injective into `ℕ`.

decls.statement: instance : Inhabited St

decls.name: HasDouble
decls.statement: def HasDouble : Option ℕ → ℕ → Prop
decls.doc: Whether the doubling edge out of the ladder state `j` is present.

decls.statement: instance : ∀ (cap : Option ℕ) (j : ℕ), Decidable (HasDouble cap j) | none, _ => .isTrue trivial | some K, j => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (2 * j ≤ K))

decls.name: hasDouble_none
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem hasDouble_none (j : ℕ) : HasDouble none j

decls.name: hasDouble_some
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem hasDouble_some (K j : ℕ) : HasDouble (some K) j ↔ 2 * j ≤ K

decls.name: hasDouble_mono
decls.statement: theorem hasDouble_mono {cap : Option ℕ} {m j : ℕ} (h : HasDouble cap m) (hj : j ≤ m) : HasDouble cap j
decls.doc: The doubling edge survives downward: if it is present at `m` it is present at every `j ≤ m`.

decls.name: OnChain
decls.statement: def OnChain : Option ℕ → St → Prop
decls.doc: The states of the chain in play.

decls.statement: instance : ∀ (cap : Option ℕ) (x : St), Decidable (OnChain cap x) | none, _ => .isTrue trivial | some K, .lad j => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (j ≤ K)) | some _, .sink => .isTrue trivial

decls.name: onChain_none
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem onChain_none (x : St) : OnChain none x

decls.name: onChain_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem onChain_sink (cap : Option ℕ) : OnChain cap .sink

decls.name: onChain_some_lad
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem onChain_some_lad (K j : ℕ) : OnChain (some K) (.lad j) ↔ j ≤ K

decls.name: onChain_double
decls.statement: theorem onChain_double {cap : Option ℕ} {j : ℕ} (h : HasDouble cap j) : OnChain cap (.lad (2 * j))
decls.doc: Where a surviving doubling edge lands is on the chain: on the truncation that is exactly the content of `HasDouble`, `2j ≤ K`.

decls.name: onChain_lad_of_hasDouble
decls.statement: theorem onChain_lad_of_hasDouble {cap : Option ℕ} {m j : ℕ} (h : HasDouble cap m) (hj : j ≤ m) : OnChain cap (.lad j)
decls.doc: A ladder state at or below a state carrying its doubling edge is on the chain.

decls.name: window
decls.statement: def window (m : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
decls.doc: The cut window `W(m) = {⌈m/2⌉, …, m−1}` of `eq:doubling_window`.

decls.name: mem_window
decls.statement: theorem mem_window {m j : ℕ} : j ∈ window m ↔ (m + 1) / 2 ≤ j ∧ j < m

decls.name: window_lt
decls.statement: theorem window_lt {m j : ℕ} (h : j ∈ window m) : j < m

decls.name: Setting
decls.statement: structure Setting
decls.doc: The standing hypotheses of `def:doubling_setting`, minus the family.

decls.name: jbar
decls.statement: noncomputable def jbar : ℝ
decls.doc: `j̄`, the mean of the target row (`def:doubling_setting`).

decls.name: epsMax_pos
decls.statement: theorem epsMax_pos : 0 < S.epsMax

decls.name: eps_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem eps_lt_one ⦃j : ℕ⦄ (hj : 1 ≤ j) : S.eps j < 1

decls.name: one_sub_eps_pos
decls.statement: theorem one_sub_eps_pos ⦃j : ℕ⦄ (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 < 1 - S.eps j

decls.name: pstar
decls.statement: noncomputable def pstar (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (f : St → ℝ) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: The function action `(P⋆ f)(x) = E(f(X₁) | X₀ = x)` of the backward kernel, in closed form.

decls.name: pstar_src
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem pstar_src : pstar S cap f .src = f .sink

decls.name: pstar_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem pstar_sink : pstar S cap f .sink = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d, S.row k * f (.lad k)

decls.name: pstar_lad_succ
decls.statement: theorem pstar_lad_succ (j : ℕ) : pstar S cap f (.lad (j + 1)) = if HasDouble cap (j + 1) then S.eps (j + 1) * f (.lad (2 * (j + 1))) + (1 - S.eps (j + 1)) * f (.lad j) else f (.lad j)

decls.name: pstar_lad_of_hasDouble
decls.statement: theorem pstar_lad_of_hasDouble {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) (h : HasDouble cap j) : pstar S cap f (.lad j) = S.eps j * f (.lad (2 * j)) + (1 - S.eps j) * f (.lad (j - 1))
decls.doc: The doubling case of `pstar`, stated at a ladder index `j ≥ 1` rather than at `j + 1`.

decls.name: pstar_lad_of_not_hasDouble
decls.statement: theorem pstar_lad_of_not_hasDouble {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) (h : ¬ HasDouble cap j) : pstar S cap f (.lad j) = f (.lad (j - 1))
decls.doc: The truncated case of `pstar`: with the doubling edge deleted, the decrement carries `1`.

decls.name: pstar_add
decls.statement: theorem pstar_add : pstar S cap (f + g) = pstar S cap f + pstar S cap g

decls.name: pstar_smul
decls.statement: theorem pstar_smul (c : ℝ) : pstar S cap (c • f) = c • pstar S cap f

decls.name: pstar_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem pstar_nonneg (hf : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) (x : St) : 0 ≤ pstar S cap f x
decls.doc: `P⋆` preserves non-negativity: it is an average over the one-step law.

decls.name: pstar_bounded
decls.statement: theorem pstar_bounded {C : ℝ} (hC : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) (x : St) : |pstar S cap f x| ≤ C
decls.doc: `P⋆` is a contraction of the sup norm: it is an average, so it cannot enlarge the range.

decls.name: pstar_const
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem pstar_const (c : ℝ) : pstar S cap (fun _ => c) = fun _ => c
decls.doc: `P⋆` fixes the constants: the rows are probabilities.

decls.name: Stat
decls.statement: structure Stat (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ)
decls.doc: An invariant probability of the chain in play — `λ` of `def:doubling_setting`.

decls.name: summable_mul
decls.statement: theorem summable_mul {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : Summable (fun x => L.lam x * f x)
decls.doc: `λ · f` is summable whenever `f` is bounded — the workhorse behind every `tsum` manipulation in the norm estimates.

decls.name: tsum_sub_pstar
decls.statement: theorem tsum_sub_pstar {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : ∑' x, L.lam x * (f x - pstar S cap f x) = 0
decls.doc: The invariance identity, rearranged: the `λ`-integral of the flow-matching defect `(Id − P⋆)f` vanishes for every bounded `f`.

files.title: `theo:doubling_sharp`: the rescaled profile converges, and its limit is determined
variables: variable {d L : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ c₃ : ℝ}

decls.name: cutBal_unique
decls.statement: theorem cutBal_unique {d : ℕ} {lam lam' : ℕ → ℝ} (h : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (h' : D.CutBal d lam' ⊤) (hagree : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ d → lam j = lam' j) : ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → lam m = lam' m
decls.doc: **Fifth bullet of the proof of `theo:doubling_sharp`.** Two sequences satisfying `eq:doubling_cut` at every `m > d` and agreeing on `λ_1,…,λ_d` agree everywhere; so `c`, `d` and the boundary data determine the whole sequence, and with it the limit `C`.

decls.name: descP_diff_eq
decls.statement: theorem descP_diff_eq {ℓ : ℕ} (u : ℕ → ℝ) {y y' : ℕ} (hy : ℓ ≤ y) (hy' : ℓ ≤ y') : D.descP ℓ u y - D.descP ℓ u y' = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ), u k * (D.exitLaw ℓ y k - D.exitLaw ℓ y' k)
decls.doc: The difference of two descent averages, as one sum against the difference of the exit laws.

decls.name: descP_uu_diff_le
decls.statement: theorem descP_uu_diff_le (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 20 ≤ ℓ) (hℓτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (ℓ : ℝ)) (i : ℕ) {m m' : ℕ} (hm : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m) (hm' : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m') : |D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) m - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) m'| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i
decls.doc: **The coupling step.** Two descent averages of the profile, started above `2^iℓ`, differ by at most `c₂(1−ω)^i`.

decls.name: uu_sub_descP_le
decls.statement: theorem uu_sub_descP_le (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hLd : d < 2 * L) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hc₂ : 0 ≤ c₂) (hweight : ∀ ℓ y : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ℓ) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : L ≤ ℓ) (y : ℕ) : |D.uu lam y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ℓ
decls.doc: **The weight step.** The profile differs from its own descent average by at most `c₂c₃/ℓ`.

decls.name: uu_diff_le
decls.statement: theorem uu_diff_le (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hLd : d < 2 * L) (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hLτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) (hweight : ∀ ℓ y : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ℓ) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : L ≤ ℓ) (i : ℕ) {m m' : ℕ} (hm : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m) (hm' : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m') : |D.uu lam m - D.uu lam m'| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ℓ)
decls.doc: **The two bullets of the proof of `theo:doubling_sharp`, merged.** At every level `ℓ ≥ L` and every `i`, two indices above `2^iℓ` have profiles differing by at most `c₂(1−ω)^i + 2c₂c₃/ℓ` — the paper's `3c₂c₃/ℓ`, improved to `2`.

decls.name: sharp_limit
decls.statement: theorem sharp_limit (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hLd : d < 2 * L) (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hLτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) (hweight : ∀ ℓ y : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ℓ) : ∃ C : ℝ, Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => D.uu lam m) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧ c₁ ≤ C ∧ C ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ ℓ i m : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ℓ)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sharp`.** The rescaled profile `u_m = λ_m m^{p_*}` converges; its limit lies in `[c₁,c₂]`; and the convergence carries the explicit error `c₂(1−ω)^i + 2c₂c₃/ℓ` at every level `ℓ ≥ L` and every `i` with `2^iℓ ≤ m`.

files.title: `theo:doubling_sharp`, unconditional

decls.name: uu_bounded_of_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem uu_bounded_of_cutBal {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (h : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hpos : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) (hℓ : D.m0 d ≤ ℓ) : ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_decay`(2) in the `u` variable, unconditional.** The same preamble as `Product.decay_two_sided_of_cutBal`, stopped one step earlier: it is the rescaled profile, not the sequence, that `Sharp.lean` takes bounds on.

decls.name: sharp_of_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem sharp_of_cutBal {d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hpos : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) : ∃ C c₁ c₂ c₆ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ C ∧ C ≤ c₂ ∧ 0 < c₆ ∧ (∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) ∧ Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → |lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p - C| ≤ c₆ * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_sharp`, with no hypothesis beyond the cut balance and positivity.** `eq:doubling_sharp` is the convergence, `eq:doubling_rate` the bound with `ϑ = Decay.vartheta`, and `c₁ ≤ C ≤ c₂` records the limit inside the decay window that `theo:doubling_decay`(2) produces.

decls.name: levelL
decls.statement: noncomputable def levelL (D : Decay) (d : ℕ) : ℕ
decls.doc: **The level of the sharp block**, `L = max(ℓ₃, 20, d+1, m₀(d), ⌈32cτ⌉)`: past it every hypothesis of `Sharp.sharp_limit` and `Decay.weight_bound` holds.

decls.name: c6
decls.statement: noncomputable def c6 (D : Decay) (d : ℕ) (c₂ : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`c₆` of `eq:doubling_rate`, written out**: `c₂(4^α + 2c₃) + c₂ m₃^ϑ` with `m₃ = max(1, ⌈L^{1/ϑ}⌉)`, `L = levelL d` and `c₂` the upper decay constant.

decls.name: sharp_explicit
decls.statement: theorem sharp_explicit {d ℓ : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hℓ : D.m0 d ≤ ℓ) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b) : ∃ C : ℝ, a * Real.exp (-(D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ))) ≤ C ∧ C ≤ b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ)) ∧ Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → |lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p - C| ≤ D.c6 d (b * Real.exp (D.c5 * (16 * D.c * D.tau) / (ℓ : ℝ))) * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_sharp` with every constant written out.** If the rescaled profile lies in `[a, b]` on the initial block `1 ≤ j < 2ℓ`, `ℓ ≥ m₀`, `a > 0`, then the limit `C` lies in `[a e^{−c₅c₄/ℓ}, b e^{c₅c₄/ℓ}]`, `c₄ = 16cτ`, and `|λ_m m^{p_*} − C| ≤ c₆ m^{−ϑ}` at every `m ≥ 1` with `c₆ = c6 d (b e^{c₅c₄/ℓ})` — a formula in `c`, `d` and the initial block, which is the paper's dependence clause "`c₆` depends on `c`, `d`, `λ_1..λ_{2m₀}` alone" made precise.

files.title: `eq:doubling_rate`: the sharp asymptotic carries a polynomial rate
variables: variable {d L : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ c₃ C : ℝ}

decls.name: alph
decls.statement: noncomputable def alph : ℝ
decls.doc: `α := log₂(1/(1−ω))`, the paper's exponent parameter.

decls.name: vartheta
decls.statement: noncomputable def vartheta : ℝ
decls.doc: `ϑ := α/(1+α)`, the rate exponent of `eq:doubling_rate`.

decls.name: one_sub_omeg_pos
decls.statement: theorem one_sub_omeg_pos : 0 < 1 - D.omeg

decls.name: one_sub_omeg_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem one_sub_omeg_lt_one : 1 - D.omeg < 1

decls.name: alph_pos
decls.statement: theorem alph_pos : 0 < D.alph

decls.name: two_rpow_neg_alph
decls.statement: theorem two_rpow_neg_alph : (2 : ℝ) ^ (-D.alph) = 1 - D.omeg

decls.name: vartheta_pos
decls.statement: theorem vartheta_pos : 0 < D.vartheta

decls.name: vartheta_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem vartheta_lt_one : D.vartheta < 1

decls.name: alph_mul_one_sub
decls.statement: theorem alph_mul_one_sub : D.alph * (1 - D.vartheta) = D.vartheta
decls.doc: `α(1 − ϑ) = ϑ`, the identity the rate turns on.

decls.name: rate_of_large
decls.statement: theorem rate_of_large (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hc₂ : 0 < c₂) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hCbound : ∀ ℓ i m : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ℓ)) {m : ℕ} (hm1 : 1 ≤ m) (hmL : (L : ℝ) ≤ (m : ℝ) ^ D.vartheta) : |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (4 ^ D.alph + 2 * c₃) * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **The rate at a large index.** At every `m` with `L ≤ m^ϑ`, the level `ℓ := ⌈m^ϑ⌉` and the index `i := ⌊log₂(m/ℓ)⌋` turn `Sharp.sharp_limit`'s error into `c₂(4^α + 2c₃) m^{−ϑ}`.

decls.name: sharp_rate_explicit
decls.statement: theorem sharp_rate_explicit (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) (hC1 : c₁ ≤ C) (hC2 : C ≤ c₂) (hCbound : ∀ ℓ i m : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ℓ)) : ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ (c₂ * (4 ^ D.alph + 2 * c₃) + c₂ * ((max 1 ⌈(L : ℝ) ^ (1 / D.vartheta)⌉₊ : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ D.vartheta) * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_rate`, with the constant written out.** With `ϑ = α/(1+α)`, `α = log₂(1/(1−ω))` and `m₃ = max(1, ⌈L^{1/ϑ}⌉)`, `|λ_m m^{p_*} − C| ≤ (c₂(4^α + 2c₃) + c₂ m₃^ϑ) m^{−ϑ}` at every `m ≥ 1`.

decls.name: sharp_rate
decls.statement: theorem sharp_rate (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) (hC1 : c₁ ≤ C) (hC2 : C ≤ c₂) (hCbound : ∀ ℓ i m : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₂ * (1 - D.omeg) ^ i + 2 * (c₂ * c₃ / ℓ)) : ∃ c₆ : ℝ, 0 < c₆ ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → |D.uu lam m - C| ≤ c₆ * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_rate`.** There is `c₆ > 0` with `|λ_m m^{p_*} − C| ≤ c₆ m^{−ϑ}` at every `m ≥ 1`: the existential reading of `sharp_rate_explicit`.

decls.name: sharp
decls.statement: theorem sharp (hcut : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hLd : d < 2 * L) (hL : 20 ≤ L) (hLτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₃ : 0 ≤ c₃) (hbd : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂) (hweight : ∀ ℓ y : ℕ, L ≤ ℓ → 2 * ℓ ≤ y → |D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) y - D.descP ℓ (D.uu lam) y| ≤ c₂ * c₃ / ℓ) : ∃ C c₆ : ℝ, 0 < c₆ ∧ c₁ ≤ C ∧ C ≤ c₂ ∧ Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → |lam m * (m : ℝ) ^ D.p - C| ≤ c₆ * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.vartheta)
decls.doc: **`theo:doubling_sharp`, assembled.** The rescaled profile `λ_m m^{p_*}` converges to a limit `C ∈ [c₁,c₂]` — this is `eq:doubling_sharp` — and the convergence carries the polynomial rate `eq:doubling_rate` with the paper's exponent `ϑ = α/(1+α)`, `α = log₂(1/(1−ω))`.

files.title: `lem:doubling_escape`, Step 2: the sojourn in a dyadic block

decls.name: pk
decls.statement: noncomputable def pk (z j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The transition law of `lem:doubling_descent`.** `P(Y₁ = j | Y₀ = z) = w_z(j)/R₀(z)` for `j ∈ W(z)`.

decls.name: half_le_R0
decls.statement: theorem half_le_R0 (hz : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) : 1 / 2 ≤ D.R0 z
decls.doc: `R₀(z) ≥ ½` above the threshold: `eq:doubling_R0`, first half.

decls.name: pk_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem pk_nonneg (hz : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) {j : ℕ} (hj : j ∈ window z) : 0 ≤ D.pk z j

decls.name: sum_pk
decls.statement: theorem sum_pk (hz : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) : ∑ j ∈ window z, D.pk z j = 1
decls.doc: The transition law is a probability on `W(z)`: `Σ_{j ∈ W(z)} w_z(j)/R₀(z) = 1`.

decls.name: escape_pk
decls.statement: theorem escape_pk (hz : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) : D.gam ≤ ∑ j ∈ halveIco z, D.pk z j
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_escape` as a mass.** `Σ_{j ≤ y/√2} P(Y₁ = j | Y₀ = y) ≥ γ`.

decls.name: halveIco_subset
decls.statement: theorem halveIco_subset (hz : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) : halveIco z ⊆ window z

decls.name: indB
decls.statement: noncomputable def indB (L z : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The indicator of the block `I = [L, 2L)`; `I_i(ℓ)` at `L = 2^i ℓ`.

decls.name: indB_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem indB_nonneg (L z : ℕ) : 0 ≤ indB L z

decls.name: indB_le_one
decls.statement: theorem indB_le_one (L z : ℕ) : indB L z ≤ 1

decls.name: indB_eq_zero
decls.statement: theorem indB_eq_zero {L z : ℕ} (h : z < L) : indB L z = 0

decls.name: halve_halve_lt
decls.statement: theorem halve_halve_lt {L z j k : ℕ} (hzthr : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (z : ℝ)) (hjthr : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (j : ℝ)) (hz2 : z < 2 * L) (hj : j ∈ halveIco z) (hk : k ∈ halveIco j) : k < L
decls.doc: **Two halvings leave the block.** If `j ≤ z/√2`, `k ≤ j/√2` and `z < 2L`, then `k < L`.

decls.name: inner_le
decls.statement: theorem inner_le {L j : ℕ} (hjthr : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (j : ℝ)) (hout : ∀ k ∈ halveIco j, k < L) : ∑ k ∈ window j, D.pk j k * indB L k ≤ 1 - D.gam
decls.doc: **One step out of the block, from an already halved state.** If every halving of `j` leaves the block, then the chance of staying in it at the next step is at most `1 − γ`.

decls.name: two_step
decls.statement: theorem two_step {L z : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hz1 : L ≤ z) (hz2 : z < 2 * L) : ∑ j ∈ window z, D.pk z j * (indB L j * ∑ k ∈ window j, D.pk j k * indB L k) ≤ 1 - D.gam ^ 2
decls.doc: **The two-step estimate.** `P(Y₂ ∈ I | Y₀ = z) ≤ 1 − γ²` for every `z ∈ I = [L, 2L)`.

decls.name: surv
decls.statement: noncomputable def surv (D : Decay) (L : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ
decls.doc: **`P(ς > r | Y₀ = z)`**, where `ς` is the exit time from `I = [L, 2L)`, as the recursion in the number of steps that characterises it: `{ς > r} = {Y₀, …, Y_r ∈ I}`.

decls.name: surv_zero
decls.statement: theorem surv_zero (L z : ℕ) : D.surv L 0 z = indB L z

decls.name: surv_succ
decls.statement: theorem surv_succ (L r z : ℕ) : D.surv L (r + 1) z = indB L z * ∑ j ∈ window z, D.pk z j * D.surv L r j

decls.name: surv_of_out
decls.statement: theorem surv_of_out {L z : ℕ} (h : ¬ (L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L)) (r : ℕ) : D.surv L r z = 0

decls.name: surv_eq_zero_of_lt
decls.statement: theorem surv_eq_zero_of_lt {L : ℕ} : ∀ (r z : ℕ), z < L + r → D.surv L r z = 0
decls.doc: The descent falls by at least one at each step, so it cannot stay in a block of width `L` for `L` steps: `surv L r z = 0` as soon as `z < L + r`.

decls.name: surv_two_pow
decls.statement: theorem surv_two_pow {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) : ∀ (r z : ℕ), D.surv L (2 * r) z ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r * indB L z
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sojourn`, first line.** `P(ς > 2r | Y₀ = y) ≤ (1 − γ²)^r`, and — the sharper form the induction needs — the bound is carried by the block indicator.

decls.name: surv_le_pow
decls.statement: theorem surv_le_pow {L z : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hz1 : L ≤ z) (hz2 : z < 2 * L) (r : ℕ) : D.surv L (2 * r) z ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sojourn`, first line, as stated in the paper.**

decls.name: geom_sum_le_inv
decls.statement: theorem geom_sum_le_inv {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x < 1) (n : ℕ) : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, x ^ i ≤ 1 / (1 - x)

decls.name: surv_antitone
decls.statement: theorem surv_antitone {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) : ∀ (r z : ℕ), D.surv L (r + 1) z ≤ D.surv L r z
decls.doc: `P(ς > r)` is non-increasing in `r`.

decls.name: surv_two_pow_le
decls.statement: theorem surv_two_pow_le {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (m z : ℕ) : D.surv L (2 * m) z ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ m
decls.doc: `P(ς > 2m | Y₀ = z) ≤ (1−γ²)^m` at every state, the indicator dropped.

decls.name: surv_partial_sum
decls.statement: theorem surv_partial_sum {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (z : ℕ) : ∀ R : ℕ, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (2 * R), D.surv L n z ≤ 2 * ∑ r ∈ Finset.range R, (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r
decls.doc: Consecutive terms of the tail sum, paired: this is the paper's `ς̃ = ⌈ς/2⌉`.

decls.name: Decay.sojMean
decls.statement: noncomputable def Decay.sojMean (D : Decay) (L : ℕ) (z : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`E(ς | Y₀ = z)`**, the expected sojourn in `I = [L,2L)`, as the recursion that characterises it: leave at once outside the block, else one step plus the expectation after it.

decls.name: Decay.sojGF
decls.statement: noncomputable def Decay.sojGF (D : Decay) (L : ℕ) (zeta : ℝ) (z : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`E(ζ^ς | Y₀ = z)`**, as the recursion that characterises it.

decls.name: c5
decls.statement: noncomputable def c5 : ℝ
decls.doc: **`c₅ := 6/γ²`** of `lem:doubling_escape`.

decls.name: sojMean_of_out
decls.statement: theorem sojMean_of_out {L z : ℕ} (h : ¬ (L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L)) : D.sojMean L z = 0

decls.name: sojMean_of_in
decls.statement: theorem sojMean_of_in {L z : ℕ} (h : L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L) : D.sojMean L z = 1 + ∑ j ∈ window z, D.pk z j * D.sojMean L j

decls.name: sojMean_eq_sum
decls.statement: theorem sojMean_eq_sum {L : ℕ} : ∀ (z N : ℕ), z < L + N → D.sojMean L z = ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, D.surv L n z
decls.doc: **The tail formula.** `E(ς) = Σ_{n<N} P(ς > n)` for every `N` past the block width — proved from the two recursions, not assumed.

decls.name: sojMean_le
decls.statement: theorem sojMean_le {L z : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hz2 : z < 2 * L) : D.sojMean L z ≤ 2 / D.gam ^ 2
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sojourn`, second line.** `E(ς | Y₀ = y) ≤ 2/γ²`.

decls.name: sojGF_of_out
decls.statement: theorem sojGF_of_out {L : ℕ} {zeta : ℝ} {z : ℕ} (h : ¬ (L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L)) : D.sojGF L zeta z = 1

decls.name: sojGF_of_in
decls.statement: theorem sojGF_of_in {L : ℕ} {zeta : ℝ} {z : ℕ} (h : L ≤ z ∧ z < 2 * L) : D.sojGF L zeta z = zeta * ∑ j ∈ window z, D.pk z j * D.sojGF L zeta j

decls.name: sojGF_eq_sum
decls.statement: theorem sojGF_eq_sum {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (zeta : ℝ) : ∀ (z N : ℕ), z < L + N → D.sojGF L zeta z = 1 + (zeta - 1) * ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, zeta ^ n * D.surv L n z
decls.doc: **The paper's expansion `ζ^ς = 1 + (ζ−1) Σ_{n<ς} ζⁿ`, in expectation.**

decls.name: surv_partial_zeta
decls.statement: theorem surv_partial_zeta {L : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (z : ℕ) {zeta : ℝ} (hz : 1 ≤ zeta) : ∀ R : ℕ, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (2 * R), zeta ^ n * D.surv L n z ≤ (1 + zeta) * ∑ r ∈ Finset.range R, (zeta ^ 2 * (1 - D.gam ^ 2)) ^ r
decls.doc: The `ζ`-weighted tail sum, paired two by two.

decls.name: sojGF_le
decls.statement: theorem sojGF_le {L z : ℕ} (hL : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (L : ℝ)) (hz2 : z < 2 * L) {zeta : ℝ} (h1 : 1 ≤ zeta) (h2 : zeta ≤ 1 + D.gam ^ 2 / 6) : D.sojGF L zeta z ≤ 1 + D.c5 * (zeta - 1)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sojourn`, third line.** `E(ζ^ς | Y₀ = y) ≤ 1 + c₅(ζ−1)` for `1 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 + γ²/6`, with `c₅ = 6/γ²`.

decls.name: thr_of_block
decls.statement: theorem thr_of_block {d ℓ i : ℕ} (hℓ : D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ ((2 ^ i * ℓ : ℕ) : ℝ)
decls.doc: The threshold holds on `I_i(ℓ)` for `i ≥ 1` and `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂`, since `2^i ℓ ≥ 2ℓ ≥ 32cτ`.

decls.name: sojourn_block
decls.statement: theorem sojourn_block {d ℓ i : ℕ} (hℓ : D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) {y : ℕ} (hy : y ∈ block i ℓ) : (∀ r : ℕ, D.surv (2 ^ i * ℓ) (2 * r) y ≤ (1 - D.gam ^ 2) ^ r) ∧ D.sojMean (2 ^ i * ℓ) y ≤ 2 / D.gam ^ 2 ∧ ∀ zeta : ℝ, 1 ≤ zeta → zeta ≤ 1 + D.gam ^ 2 / 6 → D.sojGF (2 ^ i * ℓ) zeta y ≤ 1 + D.c5 * (zeta - 1)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sojourn`.** All three bounds, on the paper's own block `I_i(ℓ)` at `i ≥ 1` and `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂`, for the exit time `ς` from that block.

files.title: The loop closure carries an invariant probability at `s = 1`, `0 < c < 1`

decls.name: rowTail
decls.statement: noncomputable def rowTail (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `R(m) = Σ_{k ≥ m} P̂_B(s_f → k)`, the mass the target row sends at or above `m`.

decls.name: rowTail_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem rowTail_nonneg (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : 0 ≤ rowTail S m

decls.name: rowTail_one
decls.statement: theorem rowTail_one : rowTail S 1 = 1

decls.name: rowTail_sub
decls.statement: theorem rowTail_sub (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : rowTail S m - rowTail S (m + 1) = S.row m

decls.name: rowTail_swap
decls.statement: theorem rowTail_swap (S : Setting) (N : ℕ) : ∀ (m k : ℕ), (m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ k ∈ Finset.Icc m S.d) ↔ (m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (min N k) ∧ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d)

decls.name: sum_rowTail_le
decls.statement: theorem sum_rowTail_le (N : ℕ) : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, rowTail S m ≤ S.jbar
decls.doc: The source term contributes at most the mean `j̄` of the target row, however far the cuts are summed: each `k` is counted `min(N, k) ≤ k` times.

decls.name: statSeq
decls.statement: noncomputable def statSeq (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The invariant sequence of the loop closure: the solution of the cut balance with the target row as source term, normalised by `λ(s₀) = 1`.

decls.name: statSeq_zero
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem statSeq_zero : statSeq S 0 = 1

decls.name: statSeq_eq
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_eq {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : statSeq S m = ((∑ j ∈ window m, statSeq S j * S.eps j) + rowTail S m) / (1 - S.eps m)

decls.name: statSeq_cut
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_cut {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : statSeq S m * (1 - S.eps m) = (∑ j ∈ window m, statSeq S j * S.eps j) + rowTail S m
decls.doc: **The cut balance with the row correction.** This is `eq:doubling_cut` at every `m ≥ 1`, not only at `m > d`; the extra term is the mass the target row sends at or above `m`, and it is what makes the cut identity hold below `d` as well.

decls.name: statSeq_pos
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_pos (S : Setting) : ∀ m : ℕ, 0 < statSeq S m

decls.name: statSeq_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_nonneg (S : Setting) (m : ℕ) : 0 ≤ statSeq S m

decls.name: statSeq_partial_sum_le
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_partial_sum_le {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (N : ℕ) : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, statSeq S m ≤ S.jbar / (1 - c)
decls.doc: **Summability with the paper's constant.** `Σ_{m=1}^{N} λ_m ≤ j̄/(1−c)` at every `N` — the same number as `σ̄ ≤ j̄/(1−c)` in `lem:doubling_supersolution`, obtained from the cut balance alone.

decls.name: summable_statSeq
decls.statement: theorem summable_statSeq {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) : Summable (statSeq S)

decls.name: window_succ_sum
decls.statement: theorem window_succ_sum {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (F : ℕ → ℝ) : (∑ j ∈ window (k + 1), F j) + (if 2 ∣ k then F (k / 2) else 0) = (∑ j ∈ window k, F j) + F k
decls.doc: The window moves by one: passing from the cut at `k` to the cut at `k+1` adds the state `k` and, when `k` is even, drops the state `k/2`.

decls.name: statSeq_point
decls.statement: theorem statSeq_point (S : Setting) (k : ℕ) : statSeq S k = statSeq S (k + 1) * (1 - S.eps (k + 1)) + (if 1 ≤ k ∧ 2 ∣ k then statSeq S (k / 2) * S.eps (k / 2) else 0) + S.row k
decls.doc: **The pointwise invariance equation on the ladder.** Mass at `k` comes from the decrement out of `k+1`, from the doubling out of `k/2` when `k` is even and positive, and from the target row.

decls.name: statMeas
decls.statement: noncomputable def statMeas (S : Setting) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: The unnormalised invariant measure on `St`: `statSeq` along the ladder, `1` at the sink.

decls.name: statMeas_lad
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem statMeas_lad (j : ℕ) : statMeas S (.lad j) = statSeq S j

decls.name: statMeas_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem statMeas_sink : statMeas S .sink = 1

decls.name: statMeas_pos
decls.statement: theorem statMeas_pos (S : Setting) (x : St) : 0 < statMeas S x

decls.name: exists_stat_none
decls.statement: theorem exists_stat_none {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) : Nonempty (Stat S none)
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_phase`(3), the `0 < c < 1` half, in the form this library consumes.** The loop-closed chain at `s = 1`, `0 < c < 1` carries an invariant probability, positive at every state.

decls.name: exists_stat_of_family
decls.statement: theorem exists_stat_of_family {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (S : Setting) (hS : S.eps = epsCS c 1) : Nonempty (Stat S none)
decls.doc: The same statement with `ε` given as the family `ε_{c,1}` rather than pointwise: the form `GFNBoundsScaffold.Doubling.exists_stat_of_lt_one` states.

files.title: The cut balance is summable at `s = 1`, `0 < c < 1`

decls.name: window_swap
decls.statement: theorem window_swap (N : ℕ) : ∀ (m j : ℕ), (m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ j ∈ window m) ↔ (m ∈ Finset.Icc (j + 1) (min N (2 * j)) ∧ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N)
decls.doc: `j` lies in the window of `m` with `1 ≤ m ≤ N` exactly when `j + 1 ≤ m ≤ min(N, 2j)` and `1 ≤ j ≤ N`: the index swap behind `window_double_sum`.

decls.name: window_double_sum
decls.statement: theorem window_double_sum (N : ℕ) (F : ℕ → ℝ) : ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ∑ j ∈ window m, F j = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ((min N (2 * j) - j : ℕ) : ℝ) * F j
decls.doc: **The double-counting step.** Each ladder index `j` is carried across a cut by exactly `min(N, 2j) − j` of the windows `W(1), …, W(N)`.

decls.name: partial_sum_le
decls.statement: theorem partial_sum_le {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) {lam g : ℕ → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ j, 0 ≤ lam j) (N : ℕ) (hrec : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → m ≤ N → lam m * (1 - S.eps m) ≤ ∑ j ∈ window m, lam j * S.eps j + g m) : (1 - c) * ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, lam m ≤ ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, g m
decls.doc: **The partial-sum bound.** At `s = 1`, a non-negative sequence obeying the cut balance up to an excess `g` on `{1,…,N}` has `(1 − c) Σ_{m≤N} λ_m ≤ Σ_{m≤N} g_m`.

decls.name: cutBalance_partial_sum_le
decls.statement: theorem cutBalance_partial_sum_le {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ j, 0 ≤ lam j) (hcb : CutBalanceSeq S lam ⊤) (N : ℕ) : (1 - c) * ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, lam m ≤ ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d, lam m
decls.doc: The instance for `CutBalanceSeq`: the excess is carried by the boundary data alone, the recursion being an equality above `d`.

decls.name: summable_of_cutBalanceSeq
decls.statement: theorem summable_of_cutBalanceSeq {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hlam : ∀ j, 0 ≤ lam j) (hcb : CutBalanceSeq S lam ⊤) : Summable lam
decls.doc: **The conclusion.** At `s = 1`, `0 < c < 1`, every non-negative solution of the cut balance is summable, with the explicit bound `Σ_{j≥1} λ_j ≤ (Σ_{j≤d} λ_j)/(1−c)`.

files.title: The linear supersolution

decls.name: pstar_mono
decls.statement: theorem pstar_mono {f g : St → ℝ} (h : ∀ x, f x ≤ g x) (x : St) : pstar S cap f x ≤ pstar S cap g x
decls.doc: `P⋆` is monotone: it is an average over the one-step law.

decls.name: linSuper
decls.statement: noncomputable def linSuper (c : ℝ) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: The linear supersolution `h(j) = j/(1−c)`, with `h(s₀) = h(s_f) = 0`.

decls.name: linSuper_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem linSuper_nonneg {c : ℝ} (hc1 : c < 1) (x : St) : 0 ≤ linSuper c x

decls.name: linSuper_lad
decls.statement: theorem linSuper_lad {c : ℝ} (j : ℕ) : linSuper c (.lad j) = (j : ℝ) / (1 - c)

decls.name: linSuper_eq
decls.statement: theorem linSuper_eq {c : ℝ} (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) : linSuper c (.lad m) = 1 + pstar S cap (linSuper c) (.lad m)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_super`, Step 1.** On the loop closure, and at every state of the truncation carrying its doubling edge, `h` solves the one-step equation exactly.

decls.name: linSuper_ge
decls.statement: theorem linSuper_ge {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hD : ¬ HasDouble cap m) : 1 + pstar S cap (linSuper c) (.lad m) ≤ linSuper c (.lad m)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_super`, Step 2.** Where the doubling edge has been truncated away, `h` is a strict supersolution: the decrement carries the whole mass and `1 ≤ 1/(1−c)`.

decls.name: hitExp
decls.statement: noncomputable def hitExp (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) : ℕ → St → ℝ
decls.doc: `E(σ ∧ n | X₀ = ·)`, defined by the recursion of Step 3: `u_0 = 0`, `u_n(s₀) = 0` and `u_{n+1}(j) = 1 + E(u_n(X₁) | X₀ = j)` at a ladder state `j ≥ 1`.

decls.name: hitExp_zero
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem hitExp_zero (x : St) : hitExp S cap 0 x = 0

decls.name: hitExp_src
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem hitExp_src (n : ℕ) : hitExp S cap n (.lad 0) = 0

decls.name: hitExp_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem hitExp_sink (n : ℕ) : hitExp S cap n .sink = 0

decls.name: hitExp_succ_lad
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_succ_lad (n j : ℕ) : hitExp S cap (n + 1) (.lad (j + 1)) = 1 + pstar S cap (hitExp S cap n) (.lad (j + 1))

decls.name: hitExp_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_nonneg (n : ℕ) (x : St) : 0 ≤ hitExp S cap n x

decls.name: hitExp_le_linSuper
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_le_linSuper {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (n : ℕ) (x : St) : hitExp S cap n x ≤ linSuper c x
decls.doc: **Step 3.** A non-negative supersolution dominates the truncated hitting expectations.

decls.name: hitExp_mono
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_mono {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) (x : St) : hitExp S cap n x ≤ hitExp S cap m x
decls.doc: The truncated hitting expectations increase in `n` — `σ ∧ n ↑ σ`.

decls.name: hitExp_iSup_le
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_iSup_le {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (x : St) : ⨆ n, hitExp S cap n x ≤ linSuper c x
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_supersolution`, the conclusion.** `E(σ | X₀ = j) ≤ j/(1−c) < +∞` on both chains: the supremum of the truncated hitting expectations is bounded by the supersolution.

decls.name: sigmaBar_le
decls.statement: theorem sigmaBar_le {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (n : ℕ) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d, S.row k * hitExp S cap n (.lad k) ≤ S.jbar / (1 - c)
decls.doc: **`σ̄ ≤ j̄/(1−c)`.** Averaging the bound over the target row, whose mean is `j̄`.

files.title: The tail of the invariant measure

decls.name: rpow_ge_tangent
decls.statement: theorem rpow_ge_tangent {q u : ℝ} (hq : q ≤ 0) (hu : 0 < u) : 1 + q * (u - 1) ≤ u ^ q
decls.doc: The tangent-line inequality for a non-positive exponent: `u^q ≥ 1 + q(u−1)`.

decls.name: incr_le
decls.statement: theorem incr_le {t : ℝ} (hp : 1 < p) (ht : 0 < t) : t ^ (1 - p) - (t + 1) ^ (1 - p) ≤ (p - 1) * t ^ (-p)
decls.doc: **The upper increment.** `j^{1−p} − (j+1)^{1−p} ≤ (p−1) j^{−p}` for `j ≥ 1`, `p > 1`.

decls.name: summable_rpow_neg
decls.statement: theorem summable_rpow_neg (hp : 1 < p) : Summable fun j : ℕ => (j : ℝ) ^ (-p)
decls.doc: `j ↦ j^{−p}` is summable for `p > 1`.

decls.name: powerTail
decls.statement: noncomputable def powerTail (p : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `Σ_{j ≥ m} j^{−p}`, the tail of the pure power.

decls.name: hasSum_powerTail
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_powerTail (hp : 1 < p) (m : ℕ) : HasSum (fun k : ℕ => ((k + m : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-p)) (powerTail p m)

decls.name: powerTail_succ
decls.statement: theorem powerTail_succ (hp : 1 < p) (m : ℕ) : powerTail p m = (m : ℝ) ^ (-p) + powerTail p (m + 1)

decls.name: tendsto_shift_rpow
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_shift_rpow (hp : 1 < p) (m : ℕ) : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ((n + m : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (1 - p)) atTop (𝓝 0)
decls.doc: The vanishing of the telescoped remainder: `(m+n)^{1−p} → 0`.

decls.name: powerTail_ge
decls.statement: theorem powerTail_ge (hp : 1 < p) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : (m : ℝ) ^ (1 - p) / (p - 1) ≤ powerTail p m
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_powertail`, lower half.** `m^{1−p}/(p−1) ≤ Σ_{j≥m} j^{−p}`.

decls.name: powerTail_le
decls.statement: theorem powerTail_le (hp : 1 < p) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : powerTail p m ≤ (m : ℝ) ^ (-p) + (m : ℝ) ^ (1 - p) / (p - 1)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_powertail`, upper half.** `Σ_{j≥m} j^{−p} ≤ m^{−p} + m^{1−p}/(p−1)`.

decls.name: tailSeq
decls.statement: noncomputable def tailSeq (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `L(m) = Σ_{j ≥ m} λ_j`, the tail of the sequence.

decls.name: tail_bounds
decls.statement: theorem tail_bounds {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : c₁ * ((m : ℝ) ^ (1 - D.p) / (D.p - 1)) ≤ tailSeq lam m ∧ tailSeq lam m ≤ c₂ * ((m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) + (m : ℝ) ^ (1 - D.p) / (D.p - 1))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tailratio`, both pairs.** With `c₁ j^{−p} ≤ λ_j ≤ c₂ j^{−p}` on `j ≥ 1`, the tail and the ratio of the tail to the mass at the cut are pinned to a power and to `m`.

decls.name: tail_ratio_ge
decls.statement: theorem tail_ratio_ge {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : c₁ * (m : ℝ) * lam m ≤ c₂ * (D.p - 1) * tailSeq lam m
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tailratio`, second pair, lower half.** `c₁ m λ_m ≤ c₂(p−1) L(m)`, the denominator-free form of `L(m)/λ_m ≥ c₁ m/(c₂(p−1))`.

decls.name: tail_ratio_le
decls.statement: theorem tail_ratio_le {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : c₁ * (D.p - 1) * tailSeq lam m ≤ c₂ * D.p * (m : ℝ) * lam m
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tailratio`, second pair, upper half.** `c₁(p−1) L(m) ≤ c₂ p m λ_m`, the denominator-free form of `L(m)/λ_m ≤ c₂ p m/(c₁(p−1))`: the tail bound `tail_bounds` divided by `λ_m ≥ c₁ m^{−p}`, with `(p−1) + m ≤ p m` for `m ≥ 1`.

decls.name: tendsto_tailSeq_zero
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_tailSeq_zero {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) : Tendsto (tailSeq lam) atTop (𝓝 0)
decls.doc: **`cor:doubling_tail`, "in particular `L(m) → 0`"**, for the sequence: squeezed between `0` and `c₂(m^{−p} + m^{1−p}/(p−1)) → 0`.

decls.name: tendsto_tail_ratio_atTop
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_tail_ratio_atTop {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => tailSeq lam m / lam m) atTop atTop
decls.doc: **`cor:doubling_tail`, "in particular `L(m)/λ_m → +∞`"**, for the sequence: the ratio dominates `c₁ m/(c₂(p−1))` (`tail_ratio_ge`).

decls.name: tail_sharp
decls.statement: theorem tail_sharp {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {C t : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) {m₀ m : ℕ} (hm : m₀ ≤ m) (hm1 : 1 ≤ m) (hclose : ∀ j : ℕ, m₀ ≤ j → |lam j * (j : ℝ) ^ D.p - C| ≤ t) : |(D.p - 1) * (m : ℝ) ^ (D.p - 1) * tailSeq lam m - C| ≤ t * (1 + (D.p - 1) / (m : ℝ)) + |C| * ((D.p - 1) / (m : ℝ))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tail_sharp`, first line, in explicit form.** If the rescaled profile is within `t` of `C` past `m₀`, then `(p_*−1) m^{p_*−1} L(m)` is within `t(1 + (p_*−1)/m) + |C|(p_*−1)/m` of `C` at every `m ≥ m₀`.

decls.name: tendsto_tail_sharp
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_tail_sharp {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {C : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hlim : Tendsto (fun j : ℕ => lam j * (j : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 C)) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => (D.p - 1) * (m : ℝ) ^ (D.p - 1) * tailSeq lam m) atTop (𝓝 C)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tail_sharp`, first line, as a limit.** If the rescaled profile `λ_j j^{p_*}` converges to `C`, then `(p_*−1) m^{p_*−1} L(m) → C`, i.e.

decls.name: tendsto_tail_ratio_sharp
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_tail_ratio_sharp {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {C : ℝ} (hsum : Summable lam) (hC : 0 < C) (hpos : ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → 0 < lam m) (hlim : Tendsto (fun j : ℕ => lam j * (j : ℝ) ^ D.p) atTop (𝓝 C)) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => (D.p - 1) * tailSeq lam m / ((m : ℝ) * lam m)) atTop (𝓝 1)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_tail_sharp`, second line.** If `λ_j j^{p_*} → C > 0` then `(p_*−1) L(m)/(m λ_m) → 1`, i.e.

files.title: Total variation as a finite sum, and the Doeblin contraction

decls.name: tvOn
decls.statement: noncomputable def tvOn (F : Finset ℕ) (μ ν : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **Total variation, ½-convention.** `tvOn F μ ν = ½ ∑_{k ∈ F} |μ k − ν k|`.

decls.name: tvOn_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem tvOn_nonneg (F : Finset ℕ) (μ ν : ℕ → ℝ) : 0 ≤ tvOn F μ ν

decls.name: tvOn_self
decls.statement: theorem tvOn_self (F : Finset ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℝ) : tvOn F μ μ = 0

decls.name: tvOn_comm
decls.statement: theorem tvOn_comm (F : Finset ℕ) (μ ν : ℕ → ℝ) : tvOn F μ ν = tvOn F ν μ

decls.name: sum_abs_eq
decls.statement: theorem sum_abs_eq (F : Finset ℕ) (μ ν : ℕ → ℝ) : ∑ k ∈ F, |μ k - ν k| = 2 * tvOn F μ ν
decls.doc: The sum form: `∑_{k ∈ F} |μ k − ν k| = 2 · tvOn F μ ν`, the ½-convention read backwards.

decls.name: tvOn_le_one
decls.statement: theorem tvOn_le_one {F : Finset ℕ} {μ ν : ℕ → ℝ} (hμ : ∀ k ∈ F, 0 ≤ μ k) (hν : ∀ k ∈ F, 0 ≤ ν k) (hμs : ∑ k ∈ F, μ k = 1) (hνs : ∑ k ∈ F, ν k = 1) : tvOn F μ ν ≤ 1
decls.doc: Two probabilities carried by `F` are at total variation at most `1`.

decls.name: abs_sum_sub_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_sum_sub_le {F : Finset ℕ} {π π' f : ℕ → ℝ} {lo hi : ℝ} (hF : F.Nonempty) (hf : ∀ k ∈ F, lo ≤ f k ∧ f k ≤ hi) (hmass : ∑ k ∈ F, π k = ∑ k ∈ F, π' k) : |∑ k ∈ F, f k * (π k - π' k)| ≤ (hi - lo) * tvOn F π π'
decls.doc: **The displayed inequality of `theo:doubling_sharp`, first bullet.** `|∫ f d(π − π')| ≤ (sup f − inf f) · TV(π ‖ π')`, for `f` ranged between `lo` and `hi` on `F` and `π, π'` of equal mass.

decls.name: mix
decls.statement: noncomputable def mix (G : Finset ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (P : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ
decls.doc: The mixture `∑_{z ∈ G} μ(z) π_z`, as a function on the states.

decls.name: mix_apply
decls.statement: theorem mix_apply (G : Finset ℕ) (μ : ℕ → ℝ) (P : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : mix G μ P k = ∑ z ∈ G, μ z * P z k

decls.name: tvOn_mix_le
decls.statement: theorem tvOn_mix_le {F G : Finset ℕ} {μ μ' ν : ℕ → ℝ} {P : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ} {ω B : ℝ} (hω1 : ω < 1) (hν : ∀ z ∈ G, ν z ≤ μ z) (hν' : ∀ z ∈ G, ν z ≤ μ' z) (hνsum : ∑ z ∈ G, ν z = ω) (hμsum : ∑ z ∈ G, μ z = 1) (hμ'sum : ∑ z ∈ G, μ' z = 1) (hB : ∀ z ∈ G, ∀ z' ∈ G, tvOn F (P z) (P z') ≤ B) : tvOn F (mix G μ P) (mix G μ' P) ≤ (1 - ω) * B
decls.doc: **The Doeblin contraction.** Two probabilities on a finite `G` that both dominate one non-negative `ν` of mass `ω < 1` mix a family of laws to within `(1 − ω)` times the family's own diameter in total variation.

decls.name: geom_iterate
decls.statement: theorem geom_iterate {Δ : ℕ → ℝ} {ω : ℝ} (hω1 : ω < 1) (h0 : Δ 0 ≤ 1) (hstep : ∀ i, Δ (i + 1) ≤ (1 - ω) * Δ i) : ∀ i, Δ i ≤ (1 - ω) ^ i
decls.doc: The geometric iteration of `lem:doubling_coupling`, as pure arithmetic: a family of diameters that contracts by `(1 − ω)` at each step and starts at most `1` is at most `(1 − ω)^i`.

files.title: The truncation, and a proved `√K`

decls.name: percut_K
decls.statement: theorem percut_K {B : ℝ} {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble (some K) m) (hB : ∀ f : St → ℝ, (∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) → (∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) → L.mass 2 f ≤ B * L.mass 2 (fun x => f x - pstar S (some K) f x)) : L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m) ≤ 2 * L.lam (.lad m) * B
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_percut_K`, squared and cleared.** Every constant bounding the `L²(λ^K)` Rayleigh quotient is at least `L_K(m)(1−L_K(m)) / (2λ^K_m)`.

decls.name: finset_sum_le_tailMass
decls.statement: theorem finset_sum_le_tailMass {m b : ℕ} (hbK : b ≤ K) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc m b, L.lam (.lad j) ≤ L.tailMass m
decls.doc: A finite block of the ladder below the cap is part of the tail.

decls.name: tail_lower
decls.statement: theorem tail_lower (D : Decay) {Cm Cp : ℝ} (hC : 0 < Cm) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (h2mK : 2 * m ≤ K) (hlo : ∀ j : ℕ, m ≤ j → j ≤ 2 * m → Cm * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (.lad j)) (hhi : L.lam (.lad m) ≤ Cp * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) : Cm / (Cp * (2 : ℝ) ^ D.p) * (m : ℝ) * L.lam (.lad m) ≤ L.tailMass m
decls.doc: **Step 5.** `L_K(m) ≥ (Cm/(Cp 2^{p_*})) · m · λ^K_m`: the tail is `m` times the mass at the cut, up to the ratio of the two decay constants.

decls.name: hitInt_le
decls.statement: theorem hitInt_le {c : ℝ} (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (hc0 : 0 < c) (n : ℕ) : L.hitInt n ≤ (K : ℝ) / (1 - c)
decls.doc: On the truncation the supersolution is bounded by `K/(1−c)`, which is what makes the hitting integrals converge.

decls.name: sqrtK
decls.statement: theorem sqrtK (D : Decay) {c B Cm Cp : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) (hC : 0 < Cm) (hKd : 4 * (S.d + 1) ≤ K) (hK8 : 8 ≤ K) (hlo : ∀ j : ℕ, K / 4 ≤ j → j ≤ 2 * (K / 4) → Cm * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (.lad j)) (hhi : L.lam (.lad (K / 4)) ≤ Cp * ((K / 4 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) (hB : ∀ f : St → ℝ, (∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) → (∑' x, L.lam x * f x = 0) → L.mass 2 f ≤ B * L.mass 2 (fun x => f x - pstar S (some K) f x)) : Cm / (Cp * (2 : ℝ) ^ D.p * 16 * (2 + S.jbar / (1 - c))) * (K : ℝ) ≤ B
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_sqrtK`, squared.** Every constant bounding the `L²(λ^K)` Rayleigh quotient is at least `c₈² K`, with `c₈² = Cm / (Cp · 2^{p_*+4} · (2 + j̄/(1−c)))` — the paper's constant, since `Cp/Cm = c₉`.

decls.name: lam_ge_prev
decls.statement: theorem lam_ge_prev (L : Stat S (some K)) {i : ℕ} (hdi : S.d < i) (hD : HasDouble (some K) i) (hi2 : 2 ≤ i) : L.lam (.lad (i - 1)) * S.eps (i - 1) ≤ L.lam (.lad i)
decls.doc: **The step down, from the cut balance.** `λ_{i−1} ε(i−1) ≤ λ_i`: keeping only the term `y = i−1` of `eq:doubling_cut` at `i`, which is legitimate because `i−1 ∈ W(i)` for `i ≥ 2`.

decls.name: lam_chain_up
decls.statement: theorem lam_chain_up (L : Stat S (some K)) {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) (n : ℕ) : L.lam (.lad (j + n)) ≤ L.lam (.lad j) * ((1 - S.epsMax)⁻¹) ^ n
decls.doc: Going up the ladder: `λ_{j+n} ≤ λ_j ρ^n` with `ρ = (1 − ε_max)^{-1}`.

decls.name: lam_chain_down
decls.statement: theorem lam_chain_down (L : Stat S (some K)) {η : ℝ} (hη : 0 ≤ η) {j : ℕ} : ∀ n : ℕ, (∀ i, j ≤ i → i < j + n → S.d < i + 1 ∧ HasDouble (some K) (i + 1) ∧ 1 ≤ i ∧ η ≤ S.eps i) → L.lam (.lad j) * η ^ n ≤ L.lam (.lad (j + n))
decls.doc: Going up the ladder from below: `λ_j η^n ≤ λ_{j+n}` when `η` is a lower bound for `ε` on the range crossed.

decls.name: block_ratio
decls.statement: theorem block_ratio (D : Decay) (L : Stat S (some K)) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = D.eps j) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓd : S.d < ℓ) (hℓ1 : 1 ≤ ℓ) (h4ℓK : 4 * ℓ ≤ K) {j j' : ℕ} (hj : ℓ ≤ j) (hj2 : j < 2 * ℓ) (hj' : ℓ ≤ j') (hj'2 : j' < 2 * ℓ) : L.lam (.lad j') ≤ (((1 - S.epsMax)⁻¹) ^ ℓ + ((D.c / (2 * (ℓ : ℝ) + 1)) ^ ℓ)⁻¹) * L.lam (.lad j)
decls.doc: **The block ratio, free of `K`.** On `[ℓ, 2ℓ)` any two masses differ by at most `Q = ρ^ℓ + (η^ℓ)^{-1}`, with `ρ = (1−ε_max)^{-1}` and `η = c/(2ℓ+1)` — constants of `c` and `ℓ` alone.

decls.name: cutBalanceSeq_trunc
decls.statement: theorem cutBalanceSeq_trunc (L : Stat S (some K)) : CutBalanceSeq S (fun j => L.lam (.lad j)) ((K / 2 : ℕ) : ℕ∞)
decls.doc: The truncation's masses satisfy `eq:doubling_cut` up to `K/2`.

decls.name: decayK
decls.statement: theorem decayK (D : Decay) (L : Stat S (some K)) (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = D.eps j) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓd : S.d < ℓ) (hℓ1 : 1 ≤ ℓ) (h4ℓK : 4 * ℓ ≤ K) {Z₁ Z₂ : ℝ} (hZ1 : 0 < Z₁) (hZ2 : 0 < Z₂) (hZlo : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → Z₁ ≤ D.descOne ℓ y) (hZhi : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Z₂) : ∃ Cm Cp : ℝ, 0 < Cm ∧ Cp ≤ Z₂ / Z₁ * (2 : ℝ) ^ D.p * (((1 - S.epsMax)⁻¹) ^ ℓ + ((D.c / (2 * (ℓ : ℝ) + 1)) ^ ℓ)⁻¹) ^ 2 * Cm ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, ℓ ≤ m → m ≤ K / 2 → Cm * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (.lad m) ∧ L.lam (.lad m) ≤ Cp * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_decayK`.** Two constants sandwiching `λ^K` on `[ℓ, K/2]`, with a ratio `C⁺/C⁻ ≤ (Z₂/Z₁) 2^{p_*} Q²` **free of `K`** — which is the `c₉` of the paper, since `Q` depends on `c` and `ℓ` alone and `Z₁, Z₂` on `c` and `d` alone.

files.title: The truncation at the paper's `B̂_K`, with constants of `c`, `d` and `j̄` alone

decls.name: diffOpK
decls.statement: noncomputable def diffOpK (L : Stat S (some K)) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_Bhat` on the truncation.** `S := (Id − P⋆ + Π)^{-1} − Π` on `L²(λ^K)`, the inverse being `Ring.inverse`, which is the two-sided inverse wherever one exists (`diffOpK_resolvent`).

decls.name: bhatK
decls.statement: noncomputable def bhatK (L : Stat S (some K)) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`B̂_K := ‖S‖_{L²(λ^K)}`** (`eq:doubling_Bhat`).

decls.name: diffOpK_resolvent
decls.statement: theorem diffOpK_resolvent (L : Stat S (some K)) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) : (1 - L.pstarL2 (rowOnChain_some hdK)) * L.diffOpK hdK = 1 - L.piL2 ∧ L.diffOpK hdK * (1 - L.pstarL2 (rowOnChain_some hdK)) = 1 - L.piL2 ∧ L.piL2 * L.diffOpK hdK = 0 ∧ L.diffOpK hdK * L.piL2 = 0
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_resolvent` at the paper's `S`.** The operator `diffOpK` satisfies `(Id − P⋆)S = S(Id − P⋆) = Id − Π` and `ΠS = SΠ = 0`: `Ring.inverse` is the inverse that `Stat.exists_diffusionOp` produces.

decls.name: percut_leftInverse
decls.statement: theorem percut_leftInverse (L : Stat S (some K)) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) {Sop : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} (hS : Sop * (1 - L.pstarL2 (rowOnChain_some hdK)) = 1 - L.piL2) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hmK : m ≤ K / 2) : L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m) ≤ 2 * L.lam (.lad m) * ‖Sop‖ ^ 2
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_percut_K`, squared, at every bounded left inverse.** If `S(Id − P⋆) = Id − Π` on `L²(λ^K)` then `L_K(m)(1 − L_K(m)) ≤ 2λ^K_m ‖S‖²` at every cut `d < m ≤ K/2`.

decls.name: percut_bhatK
decls.statement: theorem percut_bhatK (L : Stat S (some K)) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hmK : m ≤ K / 2) : Real.sqrt (L.tailMass m * (1 - L.tailMass m) / (2 * L.lam (.lad m))) ≤ L.bhatK hdK
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_percut_K`, as written.** `B̂_K ≥ √(L_K(m)(1 − L_K(m)) / (2λ^K_m))` at every cut `d < m ≤ K/2`.

decls.name: Setting.withEpsMax
decls.statement: def Setting.withEpsMax (S : Setting) (e : ℝ) (he : ∀ ⦃j⦄, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j ≤ e) (he1 : e < 1) : Setting
decls.doc: The same setting with its bound `ε_max` replaced by another admissible bound.

decls.name: Stat.withEpsMax
decls.statement: def Stat.withEpsMax {cap : Option ℕ} (L : Stat S cap) (e : ℝ) (he : ∀ ⦃j⦄, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j ≤ e) (he1 : e < 1) : Stat (S.withEpsMax e he he1) cap
decls.doc: An invariant probability of `S` is one of `S.withEpsMax e`, with the same masses.

decls.name: Stat.withEpsMax_lam
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem Stat.withEpsMax_lam {cap : Option ℕ} (L : Stat S cap) (e : ℝ) (he : ∀ ⦃j⦄, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j ≤ e) (he1 : e < 1) : (L.withEpsMax e he he1).lam = L.lam
decls.doc: The transported invariant probability has the same masses.

decls.name: truncQ
decls.statement: noncomputable def truncQ (d : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The block-ratio constant `Q = (1 − c/2)^{−m₀} + ((c/(2m₀+1))^{m₀})^{−1}` of `cor:doubling_truncation` Step 4, with `ε_max = c/2` the family's supremum.

decls.name: c9Of
decls.statement: noncomputable def c9Of (d : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`c₉`** of `cor:doubling_truncation`(2): `e^{2c₅c₄/m₀} · 2^{p_*} · Q²`, with `c₄ = 16cτ`.

decls.name: K0Of
decls.statement: noncomputable def K0Of (d : ℕ) : ℕ
decls.doc: **`K₀ := 8m₀ + 2`** of `cor:doubling_truncation`(2), Step 4.

decls.name: c8Of
decls.statement: noncomputable def c8Of (d : ℕ) (jbar : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`c₈ := (2^{p_*+4} c₉ (2 + j̄/(1−c)))^{−1/2}`** of `cor:doubling_truncation`(3), Step 7.

decls.name: one_le_truncQ
decls.statement: theorem one_le_truncQ (d : ℕ) : 1 ≤ D.truncQ d

decls.name: one_le_c9Of
decls.statement: theorem one_le_c9Of (d : ℕ) : 1 ≤ D.c9Of d

decls.name: le_K0Of
decls.statement: theorem le_K0Of (d : ℕ) : d ≤ D.K0Of d
decls.doc: `K₀ ≥ d` — indeed `K₀ > d`.

decls.name: c8Of_pos
decls.statement: theorem c8Of_pos (d : ℕ) {jbar : ℝ} (hjb : 0 ≤ jbar) : 0 < D.c8Of d jbar
decls.doc: `c₈ > 0` when `j̄ ≥ 0`, which every target row has.

decls.name: decayK_explicit
decls.statement: theorem decayK_explicit (D : Decay) (hDeps : ∀ j, S.eps j = D.eps j) (hK : D.K0Of S.d ≤ K) (L : Stat S (some K)) : ∃ Cm Cp : ℝ, 0 < Cm ∧ Cm ≤ Cp ∧ Cp ≤ D.c9Of S.d * Cm ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, D.m0 S.d ≤ m → m ≤ K / 2 → Cm * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (.lad m) ∧ L.lam (.lad m) ≤ Cp * (m : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_decayK` with its constants written out.** For every `K ≥ K₀ = 8m₀ + 2` and every invariant probability `λ^K` of the truncation there are `0 < C⁻ ≤ C⁺` with `C⁺ ≤ c₉ C⁻` and `C⁻ m^{−p_*} ≤ λ^K_m ≤ C⁺ m^{−p_*}` for `m₀ ≤ m ≤ K/2`; `m₀ = D.m0 d`, `K₀ = D.K0Of d` and `c₉ = D.c9Of d` are formulas in `c`, `p_*` and `d`.

decls.name: sqrtK_explicit
